subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 1849, thousands of gold seekers traveled by wagon train from Missouri to California.
• The overland journey covered approximately 2,000 miles.
• The trip typically took four to six months to complete.
• The goal was to reach the goldfields during the California Gold Rush.
• In 2019, historian Orla Byrne retraced portions of the route to study pioneer experiences.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize how far the gold seekers traveled. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The journey to reach the California goldfields typically took four to six months.
choices.B: The goal of the 1849 journey was to reach the goldfields during the California Gold Rush.
choices.C: The gold seekers traveled by wagon train from Missouri to California—covering approximately 2,000 miles.
choices.D: Over 170 years later, historian Orla Byrne retraced portions of the route to study pioneer experiences.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer. The sentence emphasizes how far the gold seekers traveled, indicating that they traveled by wagon train from Missouri to California, covering approximately 2,000 miles.
